title: Rav Chanin son of Rav Yeiva
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: A great man in Rava’s time, as in Bava Batra 174a, where Rava said: “Who is wise enough to do such a thing, if not Rav Chanin son of Rav Yeiva?” (He removed the judge who had sent the creditor down into the borrower’s property before the creditor had made his claim against the borrower.)
Yuchasin cites Rav Chana bar Yeiva in Rav’s time. Hyman considers this correct, for his reading was that “Rav said: Who is wise enough to do,” etc., as cited in Yuchasin HaShalem.

notes.text: The parenthesis explicitly makes the judge the object of removal in Hyman’s wording. מקמיה דלתבעה means before the creditor had first claimed from the borrower, not “before him so that he would claim.” Saved Davidson Bava Batra 174a preserves the compressed סלקיה, without independently deciding every referent in Hyman’s paraphrase.
